condition: new 3 week exertional hill breathlessness after sedentary winter with normal seated respiratory rate
level_rationale: Three weeks of new breathlessness when walking up steep hills after an indoor winter in an unassessed 64-year-old adult—with a calm seated respiratory rate of 14 breaths a minute today—warrants an initial general doctor evaluation to assess cardiopulmonary or hematologic causes rather than self-care or direct specialist referral, whereas counting 38 breaths a minute while sitting still today in the same 64-year-old indicates severe acute resting tachypnea and impending respiratory compromise requiring immediate Emergency Department care.

Counted 14 breaths a minute while sitting today

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Core dialect lexicon swap ('become dyspneic' vs 'gotten short winded', unhyphenated and retained in everyday_paraphrase and changed_fact) + single measured resting respiratory-rate escalation control (-cf, 14 to 38 breaths a minute sitting, L2 to L4).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 64, mostly indoor winter, 3 weeks of exertional hill breathlessness with no prior physician workup, and a measured seated respiratory rate of 14 breaths a minute today) with zero stated negatives. Changing only measured respiratory rate in fact f4 ('counted 14 breaths a minute' to 'counted 38 breaths a minute') follows Rule A's first-choice measured-value design and Rule D uniqueness, shifting care from initial primary-care physician evaluation (level 2) to Emergency Department acute tachypnea management (level 4).
